emerging_technology: Text-to-image diffusion models, with latent diffusion as the reference architecture
intended_application: Automatically generate final customer-facing product images and publish them to the retail website without individual product-detail review; not merely internal concept boards.
organization: A hypothetical U.S. small online homeware retailer with two marketing staff and an owner who approves concepts.
industry_sector: Consumer homeware retail and digital marketing
business_need: Replace external product photography and publish catalogue visuals at lower apparent production cost; actual saving and fidelity have not been measured.
users_stakeholders: Marketing staff, owner, freelance designer, customers relying on visual product information, and support/returns personnel.
adoption_posture: Aggressive/leading-edge for reversible learning; has not expressed acceptance of unreviewed or high-consequence public publication.
capabilities_constraints: Staff can edit images and compare ideas with a product catalogue. No in-house ML staff or training compute. An already trained model may be evaluated, but no vendor, model version, price, or license has been selected.
risk_consequence_context: Unreviewed generated details could materially misdescribe products to buyers; publication can create customer, reputational and operational consequences. No individual product-detail review or verified input/use permissions are in place.
management_question: Should this organization adopt or defer automatic final product-image publication without review, and what safer alternative or proof would change the recommendation?
time_horizon: Six-week management evidence-gathering horizon. No implied deployment date or forecast market-stage transition.
additional_context:
All context is hypothetical. This is a NEW alternative application, not the earlier internal-only concept-board proposal. The contemplated design replaces verified photography with generated product images and publishes them automatically without human item-level checking. The owner has not approved such a workflow. The company has no verified model/vendor, permissions, customer-image safeguards, local ROI, product-fidelity measures or business pilot. Prior Assignment 5 peer definition and the reversible-moodboard judgment apply to the internal concept case only; they cannot be generalized to automatic publication. Relevant peers, if researched, would need to use comparable customer-facing catalogue imagery. The existing manual-board and separate final-product-photography process remains available.

[D1] Everett M. Rogers. Diffusion of Innovations, 5th Edition. Publication: 2003. Observation: Theoretical framework; not a current adoption survey. https://www.simonandschuster.com/books/Diffusion-of-Innovations-5th-Edition/Everett-M-Rogers/9780743222099 Locator: Publisher-hosted excerpt: attributes of innovations; innovativeness and adopter categories; communication and social system. Population/measure: Adoption relative to other members of a specified social system, over time. Supports: Five perceived attributes: relative advantage, compatibility, complexity, trialability and observability. Categories describe relative adoption timing: innovators, early adopters, early majority, late majority and laggards. Social influence matters. Limits: Theory does not supply a present-day diffusion stage for image models. Fast follower is a managerial posture, not a sixth Rogers category.

[D2] Stability AI. Stable Diffusion Public Release. Publication: 2022-08-22. Observation: Public-release event, August 2022. https://stability.ai/news-updates/stable-diffusion-public-release Locator: Release announcement and links to weights, code and demonstration. Population/measure: A named model release; no adoption denominator. Supports: Stable Diffusion was publicly released with model weights, code and demonstration access. Limits: Availability is not repeated use, installed base, market share, profitability or present-day permission. Historical terms do not establish current terms.

[D3] Adam Grundy, Cory Breaux and Dhanapati Khatiwoda / U.S. Census Bureau. Large Firms With at Least 20 Employees Biggest AI Users. Publication: 2026-05-26. Observation: BTOS observations December 14, 2025–May 3, 2026. https://www.census.gov/library/stories/2026/05/ai-use-businesses.html Locator: AI Trends Across Sectors; survey question and November wording change. Population/measure: U.S. businesses; AI use in any business function during the past two weeks. Retail Trade is a broad sector, not a small-homeware subsample. Supports: The article reports around 14% current AI use in Retail Trade and around 17% expected use over the next six months. Limits: All AI, not text-to-image or internal mood boards. Intent is not actual use. No matched firm-size-by-homeware denominator. November 2025 wording broadened from producing goods/services to any business function; comparisons across that change require care. This is a dated May anchor, not an October rate.

[D4] Adobe / The Harris Poll. Inaugural Adobe Creators’ Toolkit Report. Publication: 2025-10-28. Observation: September 2025 fieldwork. https://news.adobe.com/news/2025/10/adobe-max-2025-creators-survey Locator: Key findings and methodology.
